project.name: common-messaging
project.description:
The transactional outbox and the idempotent-consumer inbox, extracted at M3 so that all three services can use them.
NOTE ON THE COUPLING THIS INTRODUCES, because it is the obvious objection: three services now share a library, and a change to it forces all three to rebuild. That is a real cost and it is accepted deliberately, because of WHAT is shared. This module holds INFRASTRUCTURE - "how does a row become a Kafka record" - which is identical everywhere and has no business meaning. It holds no domain type, no money, no saga state, and knows nothing about accounts, transfers or charges.
The failure mode of shared libraries in microservices is a shared DOMAIN model, where adding a field for one service's use silently changes another service's behaviour. That cannot happen here: the payload is an opaque String on the way out and an opaque String on the way in.
Each service still owns its own outbox and inbox TABLES, in its own database, created by its own Flyway migration. The schema is duplicated on purpose - one shared table would be a shared database, which is the coupling that database-per-service exists to prevent. Only the code that drives those tables is shared.
See docs/adr/0004-shared-messaging-library.md.
